subject: Reasoning
text: भार के आधार पर: P, Q से भारी है; R, S से हल्का है; T, S से भारी है लेकिन Q से हल्का है। इनमें से सबसे भारी कौन है?
explanation: भार का घटता क्रम: P > Q। T, S से भारी पर Q से हल्का है: Q > T > S। R, S से हल्का है: S > R। संपूर्ण क्रम: P > Q > T > S > R। अतः सबसे भारी P है।

subject: Reasoning
text: (UP B.Ed 2017) वृक्षों की एक पंक्ति में, एक वृक्ष दोनों सिरों से 5वें स्थान पर है। पंक्ति में कुल कितने वृक्ष हैं?
explanation: कुल वृक्ष = (बाईं ओर से स्थान) + (दाईं ओर से स्थान) - 1 = 5 + 5 - 1 = 9 वृक्ष।

subject: Reasoning
text: पांच पुस्तकें A, B, C, D और E एक के ऊपर एक रखी हैं। C, D के ऊपर है। E, A के नीचे है। D, A के ऊपर है। B, E के नीचे है। सबसे नीचे रखी पुस्तक कौन सी है?
explanation: क्रम इस प्रकार है: C > D, D > A, A > E, E > B। संपूर्ण क्रम: C > D > A > E > B। अतः सबसे नीचे पुस्तक B रखी है।

subject: Reasoning
text: लड़कियों की एक पंक्ति में, सीमा बाईं ओर से 8वीं है और रेखा दाईं ओर से 17वीं है। यदि वे दोनों आपस में स्थान बदल लें, तो सीमा बाईं ओर से 14वीं हो जाती है। पंक्ति में कुल कितनी लड़कियां हैं?
explanation: स्थान परिवर्तन के बाद सीमा का स्थान बाईं ओर से 14वां है, जो कि रेखा का पुराना स्थान (दाईं ओर से 17वां) है। कुल लड़कियां = 14 + 17 - 1 = 30।

subject: Reasoning
text: (UP B.Ed 2022) छह व्यक्ति A, B, C, D, E, F हैं। A, D से लंबा है लेकिन E से छोटा है। B, F से लंबा है लेकिन C से छोटा है। E, B से छोटा है। इनमें से सबसे लंबा कौन है?
explanation: लंबाई का क्रम: E > A > D। C > B > F। चूँकि E, B से छोटा है, तो B > E। संपूर्ण क्रम जोड़ने पर: C > B > E > A > D, F। अतः सबसे लंबा C है।

subject: Reasoning
text: 60 छात्रों की एक कक्षा में जहाँ लड़कियों की संख्या लड़कों से दोगुनी है, कमल ने ऊपर से 17वां स्थान प्राप्त किया। यदि कमल से आगे 9 लड़कियां हैं, तो उसके बाद रैंक में कितने लड़के हैं?
explanation: कुल छात्र = 60। लड़कियां = 40, लड़के = 20। कमल का स्थान ऊपर से 17वां है। कमल से आगे 9 लड़कियां हैं, अतः कमल से आगे लड़के = 17 - 1 - 9 = 7 लड़के। चूंकि कमल स्वयं एक लड़का है, वह ऊपर से 8वां लड़का है। कुल लड़के = 20। अतः कमल के बाद लड़कों की संख्या = 20 - 8 = 12 लड़के।

subject: Reasoning
text: सुरेश, दिनेश से आयु में बड़ा है। दिनेश, रमेश से छोटा है लेकिन राकेश से बड़ा है। इन चारों में सबसे छोटा कौन है?
explanation: सुरेश > दिनेश। रमेश > दिनेश। दिनेश > राकेश। अतः आयु क्रम में राकेश सबसे छोटा है क्योंकि दिनेश उससे बड़ा है और सुरेश व रमेश दोनों दिनेश से बड़े हैं।

subject: General Knowledge
text: भारत में राष्ट्रीय मतदाता दिवस कब मनाया जाता है? (UP B.Ed 2022)
explanation: राष्ट्रीय मतदाता दिवस प्रतिवर्ष 25 जनवरी को मनाया जाता है। भारत निर्वाचन आयोग की स्थापना 25 जनवरी 1950 को हुई थी, इसी उपलक्ष्य में यह दिवस मनाया जाता है।

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct form: She ___ to school every day. (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: With third-person singular subjects (she/he/it), we add 's' to the verb in Simple Present Tense. Hence 'goes' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive voice: 'They are building a new hospital.'

options.A: A new hospital is being built by them.
options.B: A new hospital was built by them.
options.C: A new hospital will be built by them.
options.D: A new hospital has been built by them.

explanation: Present Continuous Tense passive: Subject + is/are/am + being + past participle + by + object.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'To beat about the bush'? (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: 'To beat about the bush' means to talk around a subject without getting to the main point, i.e., to avoid the main topic.

subject: English Grammar
text: Select the correct sentence:
explanation: With specific past time expressions like 'yesterday', Simple Past Tense (saw) is used, not Present Perfect (have seen).

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct article: ___ honest man is respected everywhere. (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: 'An' is used before words starting with a vowel sound. 'Honest' begins with a silent 'h', so its vowel sound is /ɒ/, making 'An' the correct article.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct preposition: He is good ___ mathematics. (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: The correct preposition with 'good' when talking about skills or subjects is 'at'. 'Good at mathematics' is the correct usage.

subject: English Grammar
text: Change the voice: 'The teacher punished the student.' (UP B.Ed 2022)

options.A: The student was punished by the teacher.
options.B: The student is punished by the teacher.
options.C: The student has been punished by the teacher.
options.D: The student had been punished by the teacher.

explanation: Simple Past Active → Simple Past Passive. Object becomes subject + was/were + past participle + by + agent.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the synonym of 'Eloquent': (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: 'Eloquent' means fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing. Hence 'Fluent' is the correct synonym.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the antonym of 'Diligent': (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: 'Diligent' means careful and hardworking. Its antonym is 'Lazy', which means not willing to work hard.

subject: English Grammar
text: Convert to indirect speech: He said, 'I am happy.' (UP B.Ed 2020)

options.A: He said that he was happy.
options.B: He said that he is happy.
options.C: He said that I am happy.
options.D: He told that he was happy.

explanation: In indirect speech, 'said' remains 'said', 'I' changes to 'he', and 'am' changes to 'was' (backshift of tense).

subject: English Grammar
text: Fill in the blank with correct tense: By tomorrow, she ___ the project. (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: Future Perfect Tense is used for actions that will be completed before a specific future time. 'By tomorrow' indicates this, so 'will have completed' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the correct sentence:
explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and cannot be pluralized. It always takes a singular verb ('is').

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'Bite the bullet'? (UP B.Ed 2024)

options.B: To endure a painful situation with courage

explanation: 'Bite the bullet' means to endure a painful or difficult situation bravely without complaining.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct form: Neither of the answers ___ correct. (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: 'Neither' refers to 'not one and not the other' and is singular. It takes a singular verb ('is').

subject: English Grammar
text: Select the correct spelling:
explanation: 'Occasion' is the correct spelling. Common mistake is doubling 's' or missing double 'c'. Remember: oc-ca-sion.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct conditional: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the trip. (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: In First Conditional (real possibility), the If-clause uses Simple Present Tense: 'If it rains'. The main clause uses Future Simple.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correctly spelled word: (UP B.Ed 2022)
explanation: 'Receive' is the correct spelling. Remember the rule: 'i before e, except after c'. After 'c', 'e' comes before 'i': re-ceive.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the synonym of 'Benevolent': (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly; wishing or doing good. Its synonym is 'Charitable'.

subject: English Grammar
text: What does the phrase 'Pull someone's leg' mean?
explanation: 'Pull someone's leg' is an idiom meaning to joke with or tease someone, often by telling them something untrue as a prank.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the error: 'Each of the students have submitted their homework.' (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: 'Each' is always singular and requires a singular verb. The correct form is 'Each of the students has submitted'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct preposition: She has been waiting ___ two hours. (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: 'For' is used with a period/duration of time (two hours, three days). 'Since' is used with a point of time (since morning, since 2019).

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the antonym of 'Transparent': (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: 'Transparent' means allowing light to pass through so that objects behind can be clearly seen. Its antonym is 'Opaque', which means not transparent.

subject: English Grammar
text: Which is the correct indirect speech: She said, 'I will go tomorrow.' (UP B.Ed 2022)

options.A: She said that she will go the next day.
options.B: She said that she would go the next day.
options.C: She said that I will go the next day.
options.D: She said that she would go tomorrow.

explanation: In indirect speech: 'I' → 'she'; 'will' → 'would'; 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'. The tense shifts back (backshift).

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'Hit the sack'?
explanation: 'Hit the sack' is an informal idiom meaning to go to bed or go to sleep.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct article: He wants to be ___ engineer. (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: 'An' is used before words starting with a vowel sound. 'Engineer' starts with a vowel sound /ɛ/, so 'an' is used.

subject: English Grammar
text: Select the correct sentence using 'much' and 'many': (UP B.Ed 2023)

options.A: How many water do you need?
options.B: How much milk do you want?

explanation: 'Much' is used with uncountable nouns (milk, water, information). 'Many' is used with countable nouns (books, chairs). 'Milk' is uncountable, so 'much milk' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct tense: When I reached the station, the train ___. (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: Past Perfect Tense (had + past participle) is used for an action completed before another past action. 'Had already left' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct passive form: 'Who wrote this letter?' (UP B.Ed 2024)

options.A: By whom was this letter written?
options.C: By who was this letter written?
options.D: Whom was this letter written by?

explanation: In passive voice questions, 'Who' becomes 'By whom' and the verb changes to was/were + past participle. 'By whom was this letter written?' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correctly spelled word: (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: 'Accommodate' has double 'c' and double 'm'. A common mnemonic: it can accommodate both a double 'c' and a double 'm'.

subject: English Grammar
text: What does the idiom 'Under the weather' mean? (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: 'Under the weather' means to feel slightly ill or unwell. It's an idiomatic expression used when one is not feeling their best.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the type of sentence: 'What a beautiful painting this is!' (UP B.Ed 2018)
explanation: A sentence that expresses strong emotion or feeling is called Exclamatory. It usually starts with 'What' or 'How' and ends with '!'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct word: She gave me ___ advice on this matter. (UP B.Ed 2022)
explanation: 'Advice' is an uncountable noun, so it cannot be preceded by 'a/an'. We can say 'some advice' or just 'advice'. No article is used here.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the antonym of 'Frugal': (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: 'Frugal' means sparing or economical with money or food. Its antonym is 'Wasteful', meaning using more than necessary.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct preposition: The book is ___ the table. (UP B.Ed 2017)
explanation: 'On' is used for surfaces. Since a table has a surface, we say 'the book is on the table'. 'In' is used for enclosed spaces.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the meaning of the idiom 'The ball is in your court'? (UP B.Ed 2019)

options.B: It is your responsibility to take action

explanation: 'The ball is in your court' means it is now up to you to take action or make a decision. The responsibility has been passed to you.

subject: English Grammar
text: Convert to active voice: 'The song was sung by her.' (UP B.Ed 2020)
explanation: Simple Past Passive → Simple Past Active. 'By her' → 'She' becomes subject; 'was sung' → 'sang' (simple past). She sang the song.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct conjunction: He worked hard ___ he failed the exam. (UP B.Ed 2024)
explanation: 'But' is a coordinating conjunction used to show contrast or unexpected result. Working hard yet failing shows contrast, so 'but' is correct.

subject: English Grammar
text: Identify the error: 'He did not went to school yesterday.'
explanation: After 'did not' (auxiliary verb), the base form of the verb is used. 'Went' should be 'go'. Correct: 'He did not go to school yesterday.'

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the synonym of 'Obstinate': (UP B.Ed 2021)
explanation: 'Obstinate' means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or chosen course of action. Its synonym is 'Stubborn'.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct form: I wish I ___ a doctor. (UP B.Ed 2023)
explanation: In 'wish' clauses expressing impossible or unreal wishes in the present, 'were' is used for all persons (I/he/she/they wish + were). This is Subjunctive Mood.

subject: English Grammar
text: Choose the correct spelling: (UP B.Ed 2024)
explanation: 'Embarrassment' has double 'r' and double 's'. Remember: em-barr-ass-ment. It's a common misspelling due to the double consonants.

subject: English Grammar
text: What is the plural of the noun 'ox'? (UP B.Ed 2019)
explanation: Oxen is the irregular plural of ox. It does not follow the regular '-s' or '-es' rule. Other irregular plurals: child → children, man → men.
